channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: BoC's Macklem: Canada Q2 is looking pretty solid
item.description: The Bank of Canada (BoC) left its policy rate unchanged at 2.25% on Wednesday, as widely anticipated. Governor Tiff Macklem explained the decision in a press conference after the BoC dropped references to rate cuts within its statement.

item.title: Fed Chair Warsh: One-time change in prices isn't necessarily inflationary
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh said on Wednesday that recent inflation figures provide an imperfect measure of underlying inflation. Warsh made the remarks while testifying on the Semiannual Monetary Policy Report before the US Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy urgency and mixed data – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s warning that Japan must build a strong economy now, rejecting claims that an economic blueprint drove the JGB selloff.

item.title: Canadian Dollar shows little reaction to Bank of Canada interest rate decision
item.description: USD/CAD trades flat on Wednesday as traders show a limited reaction to the latest Bank of Canada (BoC) monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.4051, hovering near a one-month low.

item.title: Euro: Energy risks cap upside against US Dollar – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING says EUR/USD rallied on softer US CPI but warns that rising Oil and European natural gas prices limit upside. He expects EUR/USD to struggle above 1.1460/70 and potentially retreat toward 1.1360/80 if Oil gains another leg higher.

item.title: Fed’s Williams: June CPI consistent with progress on inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of New York President John Williams said on Wednesday that the latest United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) report was consistent with the inflation progress he hopes to see over the coming months.

item.title: Australian Dollar rises amid softer US PPI
item.description: AUD/USD trades higher near the 0.7000 level on Wednesday as the Australian Dollar (AUD) benefits from broad US Dollar (USD) weakness following softer-than-expected United States (US) producer inflation data.

item.title: US Dollar: Limited downside after CPI – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes the Dollar has steadied after its post-CPI slide, with US economic outperformance, a higher-for-longer Federal Reserve stance and strong foreign demand for US securities limiting further downside.

item.title: British Pound: Honeymoon risks for Pound – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses the British Pound's (GBP) strong performance, noting GBP is the second-best G10 currency over three months despite no Bank of England (BoE) hikes.

item.title: Euro finds support as soft US PPI weighs on US Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD recovers its intraday losses on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) comes under pressure after the latest US inflation data surprised to the downside. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1430 after hitting an intraday low of 1.1406.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Year-end weakness forecast against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Mauricio Une and Renan Alves note that the US Dollar (USD) ended the previous week at Brazilian Real (BRL) 5.1086, with the Brazilian Real appreciating 1.2% and ranking third among 24 emerging currencies.

item.title: Gold steadies as traders balance soft US inflation data against rising Oil prices
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges higher on Wednesday, erasing its intraday losses after softer-than-expected US Producer Price Index (PPI) data weighs on the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields.

item.title: Euro: ECB watching energy shock and expectations – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu reports that European Central Bank (ECB) officials Piero Cipollone and Martin Kocher are focused on preventing the energy shock and Middle East uncertainty from feeding broader Eurozone inflation.

item.title: United Kingdom: Market-friendly chancellor prospects – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ James Rossiter discusses UK political developments and their market implications, focusing on the race for the next Chancellor under expected Prime Minister Burnham.

item.title: Euro weakens against British Pound as Bank of England rate hike bets rise
item.description: EUR/GBP stays under pressure as reduced political uncertainty in the United Kingdom and expectations of higher Bank of England (BoE) interest rates keep the British Pound (GBP) favoured over the Euro (EUR).

item.title: United States annual producer inflation drops to 5.5% in June vs. 6.2% expected
item.description: Producer inflation in the United States, as measured by the change in the Producer Price Index (PPI), declined to 5.5% on a yearly basis in June from 6% in May, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Wednesday. This reading came in below the market expectation of 6.2%.

item.title: China: Growth outlook steady with policy support – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Hunter Chan and Shuang Ding note that China’s Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth slowed to 4.3% year-on-year, below the 4.5–5.0% target range, with domestic demand remaining soft.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Tentative flow reversal before BoC – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that selling of Canadian Dollar (CAD) accounts has eased ahead of the Bank of Canada (BoC) meeting, allowing light CAD purchases after prolonged pressure.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Softer inflation but Norges Bank still hawkish – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights broad Norwegian Krone (NOK) underperformance after Norway’s underlying inflation dropped to an 18‑month low, below Norges Bank and consensus projections.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed expectations weigh on Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes that softer US inflation has reduced expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes and pressured the US Dollar. June headline and core inflation fell more than consensus, leading markets to price out roughly half a hike by year-end.

item.title: British Pound dips below 1.3400, turns negative on the day as US Dollar picks up
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) has retraced previous gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, returning to the 1.3390 area from session highs of 1.3420 and turning negative on the daily chart.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Holds onto Tuesday’s gains amid risk-on mood
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) clings to Tuesday’s gains around 0.5820 during the European trading session on Wednesday. The Kiwi pair reflects strength in a risk-on market environment, driven by easing fears of Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes this year.

item.title: Indian Rupee holds early ground as traders dial down hawkish Fed bets
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains ground against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday after rising significantly in the last three trading days.

item.title: Canadian Dollar holds close to one-month high ahead of BoC decision
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) is facing an upward correction, with the USD/CAD currency pair sliding below the critical 1.4100 mark.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD hovers above $4,000, weighed by risk-off markets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges lower on “inside trading” on Wednesday, with price action contained within Tuesday’s range, as the pair keeps looking for direction above the $4,000 level.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC caution limits CAD losses against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny reports that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) has benefited from weaker United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) and higher Oil prices, with spreads pointing to modest further gains versus the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: British Pound: Modest UK growth and Bailey’s cautious stance – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities projects UK GDP to grow 0.1% month-on-month in May, led by services and strong retail sales, while manufacturing and industrial output remain under pressure from Middle East-related headwinds and higher input costs.

item.title: Euro gives away gains as Eurozone Industrial Production disappoints
item.description: The Euro (EUR) has given away previous gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, with the EUR/USD pair retreating to levels just above 1.1420 from session highs near 1.1450.

item.title: United States: Cool CPI provides temporary relief for rates – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Samuel Tse and Senior Rates Strategist Eugene Leow analyse USD rates after softer June CPI data. They note the US Treasuries curve bull steepened as headline and core CPI surprised to the downside, with energy and some core services prices falling.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Wednesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $58.41 per troy ounce, down 0.46% from the $58.68 it cost on Tuesday.
